questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce the chance of a crash, be visible to others, signal your intentions, keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react to changing conditions.

questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Encourage the tailgater to pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage the tailgater to pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: If you can do it safely, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Continue the passing maneuver if you see an upcoming bridge.
Continue the passing maneuver if you see an upcoming railroad crossing.
Try to pass more than one vehicle at a time to save time.
Not follow another vehicle that is passing a car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not follow another vehicle that is passing a car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Do not pass if conditions are unsafe, such as oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bridges, curves, hills, intersections, or railroad crossings. Do not pass more than one vehicle at a time. Do not follow a vehicle that is already passing.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. There is no better way to learn than by doing.
Just start riding. Most bikes are similar, so you don't need to find the safety features.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn the bike's gear pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn the bike's gear pattern.
questions.explanation: Every bike is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, check safety and maintenance, find where everything is, and practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.

questions.question: If you have only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your riding skills from the first drink. Do not ride if you have consumed any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. Stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: You can reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or reduce alcohol's effects. They may help you stay awake, but they cannot make you sober.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you. Reflective materials help even more.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Ride as fast as other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Ride at a speed where you can stop within the area lit by your headlight. Slow down when you cannot see well.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Alcohol builds up in your body when you drink fast. Your body processes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your body.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of the lane behind a car, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers check their side mirror less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can block the side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers check their side mirror less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so drivers can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see everything you need to see for safe riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see everything you need to see for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see all the sides you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What should you think about first when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: How well it protects you
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when buying a helmet. Choose one that fastens securely, fits right, and is DOT-approved.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, like car mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, like car mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When buying a helmet, focus most on the helmet's:
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a helmet.

questions.question: To avoid a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe space around your bike to avoid crashes. Maintain this space when following, being followed, passing, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black symbols tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly around your head and have no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: In a crash, a rider wearing a helmet is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than a rider without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as a rider without a helmet.
More likely to survive than a rider without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets. Speed does not change this fact.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. Speeding up will not help—they will just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Reflective or brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make motorcycle riders more visible.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you better on the road.

questions.question: Avoid riding directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: The driver may need your lane to pass another car.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have more escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver cannot see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your way to escape if a hazard appears.
